trickyParts: ReloadOptions refuses an Options whose Port or HTTPPort differs from the one the server was started with ('config reload not supported for HTTPPort: old=-1, new=52544'). Server.Reload therefore builds the new Options from the new configuration text and then restores Host, Port, HTTPPort, HTTPHost, StoreDir, NoSigs, ConfigFile and the JetStream flag from the options the server was started with, and never reads a port back from the running server. TestARefusedReloadAnswersWithTheServersReasonAndKeepsTheOldConfiguration pins it.

natsserver.ConfigureOptions leaves its parse in natsserver.FlagSnapshot, a package-level variable every later ReloadOptions in the process merges over the options it is given, whatever server they belong to. serverOptions clears it under a package flagsMu that Reload takes too, so one test binary's several servers never read each other's command line.

internal/bus/remote_nats_test.go's remoteLookingURL needed a non-loopback address of this machine that reaches the test's own server. The container published its port on 0.0.0.0; the in-process server listens on loopback alone, so the test holds that non-loopback port itself through the package's relayProxy.

Main cannot register the shared server's cleanup on the test that first asked for it: that server outlives the test, and a t.Errorf on a finished test panics. sharedTB collects the cleanups and reports to stderr and the exit code instead.
deviations: The plan's section 4.1 kept StartRestartable beside Start and said the relay would bind 0.0.0.0 for the pulumilive lane. Neither held. With every server behind the relay, Start already returns a server whose URL survives Stop and Start, so StartRestartable was two identical exported functions and is deleted; its eight call sites take Start. And infra/host/live_test.go's containers run with networkMode: host (the file says so at its head, and the inline program sets it), so loopback reaches them: the relay binds 127.0.0.1 for every caller and no reachable-address mode was needed. go vet -tags pulumilive ./... is clean in packages/envoy/infra.

The plan's T1 listed packages/envoy/infra/go.sum, packages/daemon/go.sum and go.work.sum among the files to change. None needed to: go work sync and a go mod tidy in each module produced large unrelated version moves (gorilla/websocket to a pseudo-version, protobuf 1.36.11 to 1.36.12, the daemon's s3 dropped for kms, otel and grpc bumps) that are pre-existing drift rather than this change's, so they were reverted. packages/daemon builds and vets, and packages/envoy/infra builds and vets under every tag, against the base's sums: both resolve the new module through packages/envoy/go.sum in their workspaces.

Two CI jobs beyond the plan's T5 and T6 were cleaned up, because the change makes their setup dead: envoy-go-race and dispatch-multiprocess each pre-pulled testnats.Image and envoy-go-race carried TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED for a NATS that now runs in the test process. Leaving a pre-pull step would not have failed the job, but it reads the constant for a container nothing starts.

discoveredComplexity: internal/dispatch/pmdoc's failures in a pod are not the plan's section 1.1 cause. A repository-root bun install (needed for scripts/e2e-local.sh anyway) fixed 'Cannot find module @legion/proof-editor'; what fails now are its parse and render linearity tests, which compare wall-clock ratios between input sizes (linear_test.go:216 and :274) and lose on a loaded 2-CPU pod. The ce-simplify-code pass found one correctness defect rather than the expected nothing: relay.freeze handed every overlapping freeze its own thaw over one shared gate, so a second thaw panicked the test binary with 'close of closed channel'. No caller freezes twice today, so no test showed it. It is fixed and proved by a negative control.

The guard test's migration allowance lists, written so the guard could land before the call sites moved, are spent and deleted: the guard now reports every importer and every docker-driving file it finds, with packages/envoy/infra's pulumilive lane the one allowance left in the file walk.

ROUND 2 - the pull request body's residue line for internal/dispatch/pmdoc named the wrong cause. It is not a loaded pod: the three linearity tests time work with getrusage through internal/cputest.Process (linear_test.go:372-413), and getrusage advances in 10 ms steps in this gVisor pod, so an input that takes under 10 ms reads 0s and every ratio is '+Inf times the 0s it took'. The tester reproduced it on an idle pod and the package is green in CI's envoy-go-race. The body now says so.
